scientificCorrectness.finding: Acidic vinegar cleaner reacts with carbonate in marble, with bubbling; it is unsuitable for such marble. The icon arrow to bubbles is a compact illustrative reaction, not a balanced equation or a claim that gas is the only product. No contradictory chemical depiction, fabricated measurement, numerical error or unsafe active procedure is visible.

wholeGoalAndProfileFit.finding: The whole DE/EN goal requires coherent explanation, justified argument, constructive exchange and reflection/correction of an own standpoint. The group and claim/evidence/reason/conclusion chain provide a concrete introduction to this process. This image is a static example and does not demonstrate actual responsive dialogue or an actual change of personal standpoint. That is a scope limit, not a claim of recorded performance.

bothCompleteCasesFit.finding: Catalyst and conductivity cases each require real partner contributions, responsive follow-up and explicit own reflection; model replies cannot stand for performed dialogue. The image uses a different acid/carbonate example of the same argument process, so it is not a mismatched case solution. It neither certifies mastery of those cases nor removes their criteria.

didacticMotivationAndStyle.finding: Approachable coloured comic laboratory scene, diverse peer group, everyday cleaning question and evidence-to-reason chain suit an upper-secondary process goal. The crossed-out bare opinion is understandable as requiring scientific justification. It is an orientation illustration, not an assessment. No reference pool was opened in this blind single-input review, so comparative style matching to other assets is not claimed.

actorPerspective.finding: The four upright panels are infographic overlays, not depicted worksheets being read backwards by the people.
